task: Owner-approved (dasomel) load of the Trivy security DB into the local Harbor, plus why provisioning left it empty and the repo fix. Live-verified on the local arm64 cluster; portal API check listed as not claimed where not done.

events.summary: Fix push-security-db.sh (auth, https endpoint, CA), add a repo_count WARN to 08-5, correct the display-only TRIVY_DB_REGISTRY, add R303/R304, lessons-log row. Deliberately left alone: auto-loading the DB from up.sh (needs internet and a promotion approval), trivy-operator.yaml, node-collector image mirroring, the Kakao path.

Harbor project trivy-db repo_count 0; scan Jobs NOT_FOUND on trivy-db/aquasecurity/trivy-db:2. Running the unmodified push-security-db.sh against a port-forward failed with 'server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client'; the script has no credential at all.

events.provenance: Harbor token-realm behavior observed live on the local cluster 2026-11-04: the registry token realm is https://harbor.<domain>/service/token, so a plain-HTTP push endpoint fails with 'server gave HTTP response to HTTPS client'
events.summary: The push endpoint must be Harbor's external https URL with the Narwhal CA, not the in-cluster Service.

push-security-db.sh logs in with the harbor-secrets admin credential into a 0600 authfile (xtrace suppressed around the credential), supports --ca-cert/--kube-context, defaults to harbor.${DOMAIN}; 08-5 warns when trivy-db has <3 repos; 13-2 TRIVY_DB_REGISTRY and the portal default now equal trivy-operator.yaml dbRegistry+dbRepository.

Independent review of PR #550 found the trace lacked typed passed evidence, the push script leaked the password under set -x, R303 did not require --authfile on every Harbor skopeo call, and the header comment was stale; all four fixed.
